Sakharam vs Suresh on 12 August, 2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Ind:25042
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh
 Misc. Appeal No. 141 of 2016
 Sakharam And Others
 Versus
 Suresh And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Ram Narayan Dave - Advocate for the applicants  Shri Ramesh Chandra Gangare - Advocate for the respo  and 2.
 Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain - Advocate for the respondent

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act is preferred challenging the award dated 29.09.2015 in Claim Case No. 50/2013 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Badwah for enhancement of Rupees 25,000/- compensation.

entities.text:
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Badwah
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. Facts in brief are that it is the claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was preferred seeking 20 lacs compensation for the death of 15 year old son of the petitioners.

The motor vehicle accident dated 15.02.2013 at 11:30 am with the jurisdiction of Police station Karai, Tehsil Maheshwar, District West Nimar, Mandleswar was a result of negligent driving of Tractor No. MP 10/AA/3423 by respondent No.1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:25042 2 MA-141-2016 Suresh, owned by respondent No.2 Pankaj and insured with respondent No.3.
Accordingly, income from working as Labourer stated to be Rs. 3000/- per month and it was also stated that deceased Kamlesh was student at the time of accident.

The claim was contested and Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence of Sakaram as PW-1, Gulabsingh as PW-2 and admitted the documents Exhibits-P-1 to P-8.
03.

After appreciating the evidence the Tribunal partly allowed the claim and awarded a total compensation of Rs. 2,55,000/- in the heads of loss of dependency Rs. 2,00,000/-, towards loss of love and affection Rs.30,000/-, towards funeral expenses Rs. 25,000/-
Sakharam vs Suresh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175179617/
1 04

This appeal has been preferred on the ground that the Tribunal has committed error in assessing the annual income of Rs. 50,000/- instead of Rs. 36,000/- The increase in the head of future prospects has not been taken into consideration.
Interest @12% per annum ought to have been awarded.
05. Counsel for the respondent No.3, Insurance Company opposed the prayer submitting that all the heads have been adequately compensated.

06. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
07.

ought to have been awarded in the head of filial consortium instead of awarded Rs.
30,000/-, in the head of love and affection compensation of Rs. 30,000/- ought to have been awarded in the head of loos of estate and funeral expenses instead of Rs. 25,000/.
08.
Now the question of compensation in the head of loss of dependency required to be examined.

09. In paragraph-17 of the award, Tribunal has recorded the finding NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:25042 3 MA-141-2016 that deceased do not have any regular income.
He only assist occasionally his father when he accompanied with parents to the filed and this finding is in-consonance with the Paragraph-5 of the Gulabsingh (PW-2).

The Tribunal has estimated the notional income of the Kamlesh as Rs. 15000/- per annum and deducting 1/3d for personal expenses applied the multiplier of 20 estimated loss of dependency Rs. 2,00,000/-.

In Meena Devi Vs. Nanuchand, 2022 Live Law (SC) 841, for the age of 12 years' child death the notional income was assessed Rs. 30,000/- per annum and in the case of Kusmi Devi vs. Mohd. Kasim and another, 2023 ACJ 1658 , for the death of three years old child in the accident a compensation of Rs. 6,00,000/-
was awarded and seeking global enhancement.

entities.text: Meena Devi Vs. Nanuchand, 2022 Live Law (SC) 841
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kusmi Devi vs. Mohd. Kasim and another, 2023 ACJ 1658
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. In this case considering Paragraph-3 of Sakaram (PW-1) and Paragraph-3 of Gulabsingh (PW-1)
the notional income of the deceased is assessed Rs. 36,000/- per annum and applying the multiplier of 18 a total loss of dependency come to Rs. 6,48,000/- and on recalculation a total compensation comes to Rs. 7,58,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs. 2,55,000/-.
Rest of the heads are adequately compensated.

11. With the aforesaid, this misc. appeal is allowed and total compensation of Rs.5,03,000/- (Five lac three thousand only) is further enhanced with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application ie 11.07.2013 .
The enhanced amount be satisfied and distributed as per para 20 of the award of Tribunal.

12. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:25042 4 MA-141-2016 Rs.25,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly, however,
for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of Sakharam vs Suresh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175179617/
2 compensation.
13.
Accordingly, this misc appeal is disposed of.
Pending I.As if any, shall stand closed.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE rashmi Sakharam vs Suresh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175179617/
